video.title: The Low-to-High Forehand is Mostly a Myth

classification.reason: The speaker explains the mechanics of the swing path on high balls and near the net, but does not provide any actionable drill, cue, or instruction.

problem.title_as_question: Is the low-to-high forehand swing mostly a myth?
problem.definition: The traditional concept of a low-to-high forehand swing is largely inaccurate, especially on high balls or near the net where the swing moves almost entirely back to front.

quotes.text: the low to high forehand is mostly a myth
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: especially when you're close to the net or the ball is high
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: you're swinging basically back to front
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the elevation gain is so minimal you might not even notice it
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The racket swings almost purely back to front with minimal vertical elevation gain.

causes.statement: Being close to the net or encountering a high ball requires swinging primarily back to front rather than upward.

angles.summary: Debunks the common dogma that forehands must always follow a low-to-high trajectory.
Explains that elevation gain is virtually unnoticeable on high balls or near the net as the swing is mostly back to front.
